# Scope: com.desertstormfront.ai (190 methods + 25 fields; 2 methods and the remaining state
# fields are deliberately left unnamed, see the end of this header).
# Two parallel node hierarchies with an identical shape, so one naming scheme covers both:
#   plan  (PlanNode):     b()=getName, a()=reset, c(ctx)=canRun, d(ctx)=run, b(ctx)=getActiveNode
#   behavior (BehaviorNode): a()=reset, c(bb)=canRun, d(bb)=run, b(bb)=getActiveNode (no name)
# Evidence: PlanNode/BehaviorNode declare exactly those five/four abstract members; the composites
# implement c() as "has children" and getActiveNode() as "resolve to the child that would run"
# (SelectorPlanNode/SequencePlanNode walk children, ActionPlanNode/ActionNode return themselves via
# asAction(), DecoratorNode/ConditionNodeBase forward to their single child).
#   fields a/b = children (pool/list) and activeIndex (the -1-initialised child cursor).
# DecoratorNode/ConditionNodeBase: field a = child; the new abstract a(ctx)/a(bb) asks "is the
#   condition satisfied" = isSatisfied, used by ConditionPlanNode (c()=canRun forwards to it) and
#   GuardPlanNode (run() returns SUCCESS when the guard does not hold).
# PlanContext: fields a/b/c = aiContext/commander/intent; a(Intent)=setIntent, a()=getAiContext,
# plan.nodes: every task node is (getName, reset, run) or (getName, isSatisfied) for the IsXxx
#   conditions; the monitor family (MonitorPlanBase and its LoadPlan/UnloadPlan/MonitorEngagePlan/
#   MonitorReachPlan/MoveRoguePlan/MoveToTargetPlan subclasses) splits run() - which prunes dead
#   units and fails when a transport/capturer was lost - from the abstract e(ctx)=monitor() that
#   MoveToTargetPlan: a/b(AIContext, Vec2, x, y) spiral outward from (x,y) for the nearest tile the
#   given domain can path to (Ground / Water) and return its tile index = findNearestGroundTile /
#   UnitAssignPlanBase: the four protected a(...) helpers pick the nearest unassigned/immobile unit
#   AssignGuardPlan: a(AIContext) picks a random combat type = pickCombatUnitType; fields
#   TargetSelector (a static helper, not a node): a(bb)=isFlyingUnit, b(bb)=selectTarget (chooses
#   the best reachable target by damage/distance and issues the order; also drives the fighter
#   patrol circle when nothing is in range).
#   InfluenceMap: a(w,h,cell)=create ; a() folds the raw values into the coarse cells (0.7 falloff
#   for neighbours) = rebuild ; b()=getCellSize ; a(Vec2)/a(ff)/a(ii)=getInfluence on the folded
#   grid ; a(iif)=setValue / b(ii)=getValue on the raw grid. Fields a..g = values/width/height/
#   (removes the lowest-total-health intent of that type), a(IntentType,ff)=countAt,
#   IntentGroupList: a()=hasRequests, b()=hasUnits, a(UnitType)=hasUnitOfType (same name as the
#   IntentGroup method it delegates to), c()=hasCapturingUnit, a(Unit)=findGroup.
#   influence-map refresh, one phase per call).
#   UnitRequest: fields a/b = unit/unitType ; a(Unit,UnitType)=of ; get/setUnit, get/setUnitType.
#   AIContext: s() rebuilds and returns the cached visible-enemy list = collectVisibleEnemyUnits.
# Deliberately unnamed (no evidence in this tree, left obfuscated rather than guessed):
#   AIContext.c()/a(int) and their field n (written 0 at create, no other reader); IntentGroup
#   fields a/d/g; the IntentGroupMode and NodeStatus constants (2 and 4 values, their meaning needs
#   the call sites that compare them); the per-node int/float state fields (timeouts, indices).
